name: CLN Energy Limited
sector: Lithium-ion battery pack assembly and energy-storage solutions
summary: Genuine manufacturing growth but weak recent cash conversion and collateral-intensive funding. At the dated secondary ₹463 close, a fully funded base yields only 3.32% annually against a 15% hurdle, while credible bear loss is about 85%. Conditional IAS is numerical and unfavorable; no allegation of misconduct or certain insolvency.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Avoid at the dated reference valuation, not a governance accusation. CLN has genuine manufacturing growth and usable reported profits, but two large cash-outflow years, pledged deposits and on-demand bank finance prevent calling it a cash-backed compounder. At the secondary 19 October close of ₹463, the revised funded base yields only 3.32% annually against a 15% hurdle; the credible bear loses about 85% of entry value. October equity helps, but does not finance the modeled growth path by itself. Numerical quality and conditional investment scores are now supportable; no live execution or certain forecast is claimed.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: As of 20 October 2026. BSE SME 544347, ISIN INE0WDX01010, listed 30 January 2025. Consolidated FY25–26 follows separately identified standalone restated FY22–24. ₹ crore unless stated. A dated secondary BSE close of ₹463 and primary October allotment of 10,803,250 issued shares imply ₹500.19 crore equity value; the stale interop-master capital is superseded. The 200-share lot costs ₹92,600. The five-year investor horizon ends 19 October 2031; annual FY27–31 operations plus a terminal fiscal stub use March balances and explicitly timed later capital, not a fabricated October balance sheet. The 15% equity hurdle and ₹5 lakh position are research conventions, not WACC or personal suitability. All four gates are Conditional; no unsubstantiated critical failure is imposed.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: BQS 5.36; GQS capped at 5 for persistent CASH 3. IAS 2.59 is conditional on the secondary 19 October quote, ₹5 lakh reference position and stated financing assumptions. R/D/P/L 1/2/3/2. No unsupported governance or funding override. All nine quality factors retain company-specific evidence and counterevidence. R is mechanically assigned from the −11.68 percentage-point reference-return spread. D measures the funded loss path; P measures demanding priced-in assumptions, not a second arbitrary return haircut. L starts in the 3–4 band and is explicitly reduced to 2 for lot-size and trading constraints. Every canonical weight and contribution is retained in score_audit, without missing-factor reweighting. One-point MOAT/CAP changes alter BQS by 0.20/0.12 and IAS by 0.05/0.03; they do not rescue the valuation shortfall.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: CLN assembles and engineers lithium-ion battery packs and ancillary systems for telecom backup, mobility and industrial/storage applications. It is not established as a lithium-cell manufacturer. FY26 manufacturing revenue ₹298.9951 crore, trading ₹18.2797 crore and services ₹29.0323 crore show a shift toward in-house value addition. Cells, certification, safety, warranties and collection timing determine economics. New Indian/Dubai subsidiaries contributed little historical revenue; Egyptian assembly is a new project, not proven capacity earnings. FY26 core EBITDA excluding ₹4.8199 crore other income is ₹37.4944 crore, or 10.82% of sales. Operating expenses already include warranty accrual and employee compensation. Their future cash requirements cannot be erased by adding back provisions while also treating all accounting profit as distributable cash. Existing CLNGreen has a 49% outside stake but only ₹0.555 crore revenue; the model allocates its minority consistently with the specified common operating assumptions and separately stresses a larger deduction.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Engineering, product qualification and customer integration offer moderate capability. Historical FY24 largest customer share 34.15%, top ten 73.56%, and top-ten supplier share 78.92% limit bargaining independence; these are dated, not current concentration claims. IPO peers Eveready, Panasonic Energy India, High Energy Batteries and Indo National span consumer primary batteries and specialty/defence applications, unlike CLN’s lithium-pack/telecom mix. Their FY24 metrics and January 2025 multiples are not current comparable valuations. No premium is justified solely by an EV/BESS label. Direct contemporary primary checks reinforce the limits of comparison: High Energy Batteries FY26 revenue was ₹83.53 crore, with core EBITDA before the labour-code exceptional cost of ₹19.06 crore, reflecting specialty aerospace/naval products. Eveready FY26 standalone sales were ₹1,454.61 crore and core pre-exception EBITDA ₹163.55 crore. Its ₹171.23 crore PAT includes exceptional income and substantial tax/MAT effects, so it is not a clean recurring earnings anchor. Eveready’s consumer distribution and High Energy’s specialty qualifications are not CLN’s pack-assembly moat. Panasonic and Indo National remain partial prospectus comparators; no unmatched current-price peer ranking is manufactured.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Restated standalone revenue FY22/FY23/FY24 was ₹121.6896/₹128.8194/₹132.7086 crore; group FY25/FY26 was ₹219.1796/₹346.5123 crore. The three-year CAGR from FY23 is approximately 39.1%, with the short-history score capped at REV 8. Five annual observations do not supply a five-year CAGR. FY26 CLNGreen sales of ₹0.555 crore and nil Dubai sales cannot explain most of the ₹127.33 crore annual increase. Manufacturing rose from ₹89.3682 crore in FY24 to nearly ₹299 crore in FY26, while trading’s share declined. Absolute scale and mix therefore support growth, but concentrated telecom orders, qualification and collection cycles prevent treating one strong year as guaranteed recurrence. FY23 fire loss distorts PAT comparisons. There is no invented October half-year result or seasonal annualization.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Telecom replacement, industrial storage and mobility offer a runway, but funding is the binding resource. The July 2025 BSNL update reported first-phase dispatch and a planned second-phase completion, distinguishing a ₹107.91 crore tender from a ₹77 crore PO. This is historical execution context, not new October 2026 backlog or proof of collection. August approved ₹10 crore into Dubai; September disclosed USD 2 million invested in Egypt through Dubai, with 99%/1% ownership through the subsidiary/chairman. The model uses a ₹17 crore aggregate overseas cash budget, with ₹10/25 crore bounds, rather than double-adding both announcements or claiming a verified currency conversion. No unproven foreign revenue or terminal recovery is invented. Core NOPAT of about ₹22.83 crore on broad average equity-plus-bank-debt less usable cash gives approximately 14.4%, within a reasoned 12–16% capital-cost range. Collateral remains invested capital. Exact project and acquisition-adjusted incremental ROIC are ND, not inferred from high sales growth or low physical capex.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: October 5 promoter allotment raised ₹10.575 crore at ₹423, increasing shares to 10,803,250; the official security master remains stale at 10,553,250. ESOP grant covers 160,046 shares at ₹10, treated as potential dilution. Actual subsidiary/associate loans were ₹0.366/₹0.0441 crore, but prospective subsidiary-loan terms were deferred to execution and borrowing authority proposed ₹1,000 crore is not sanctioned debt. October17 issuer disclosure concerns chairman Rajiv Seth’s personal commercial dispute in Singapore, which he contests; issuer states no CLN assets/liabilities and expects no business impact. Court and case number are not disclosed, and no misconduct finding is inferred. Minor unfinished MD&A drafting does not alone trigger G2. The July 1 board filing accepted Manish Shah’s WTD/COO resignation effective June 30 and appointed Rahul Bhatnagar and Sanni Kumar; management continuity remains an execution item, not an adverse integrity finding. The June proposal’s minimum ₹401 preferential price was superseded by actual October allotment at ₹423. Authorization is not cash until allotment, and proposed borrowing authority is not a bank sanction. The granted option pool is distinct from the larger authorized ESOP pool; the model includes 160,046 granted options, exercise cash and a no-exercise sensitivity.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY22–24 standalone CFO was ₹7.9285/₹15.0248/₹6.7713 crore, but this history included substantial supplier financing. Prospectus vendor-acceptance balances of ₹15/31/26 crore represented goods delivered ahead of schedule against future purchases, not bank borrowing or an unexplained windfall. Their runoff helps explain later cash absorption. FY25/FY26 reported CFO was −₹66.8189/−₹45.8878 crore against group PAT of ₹12.9219/₹20.5743 crore. FY26 absorption includes receivables ₹22.4212 crore, advances ₹11.4724 crore, payable reduction ₹31.0775 crore and other-current-liability reduction ₹20.3579 crore. Net PPE/intangible/development spending of ₹4.1035 crore produces reported FCF proxy −₹49.9913 crore before borrowing interest classified in financing; it is not FCFE. The five-year mixed-scope cash diagnostic is negative, with the scope limitation explicit. FY23 fire loss and FY25 insurance recovery remain separated from recurring growth.

The full opening map uses actual operating WC of ₹161.9084 crore, not a guessed percentage. Current tax of ₹8.529 crore is explicitly net of TDS and is settled once. Current net gratuity, absence and employee payables total ₹1.7245 crore; a ₹0.0001 crore rounding residual is retained conservatively. Ordinary current dues of ₹4.8673 crore and warranty reserve ₹3.1913 crore remain in operating WC and are not paid a second time. Noncurrent net employee claims ₹0.4741 crore and rent-equalization ₹0.5484 crore are retained at terminal. Plan assets are already netted, and the ₹0.2593 crore equity-settled ESOP reserve is not cash debt.

Only ₹1.495 crore cash/current accounts are used as free cash. All ₹33.3728 crore short/long deposits are restricted in the reference model; collateral grows with sales. Accrued FD interest of ₹1.762 crore is outside WC and opening cash, with old-interest recovery separately sensitized. Normal GST recoverable remains operating WC, not a second income-tax offset. Good receivables overdue six months of ₹1.0563 crore mitigate ageing concerns, while ₹43.3992 crore finished inventory and warranty experience require monitoring. Nothing here treats legitimate provisions, collateral or routine drafting differences as misconduct.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At the dated ₹463 close, market capitalization is ₹500.19 crore and FY26 owner P/E about 24.34×, using current issued shares. Core EBITDA is ₹37.4944 crore; static mixed-period EV/core EBITDA is about 15.79× before small minority and rent claims, with no pledged-deposit netting. The model uses 18% base revenue growth, 11% margin, 50% operating WC, 10% collateral, 3% revenue capex and the separate overseas budget. Depreciation, 26% positive-profit cash tax, current claims, interest and both dilution/proceeds are linked annually. New borrowing incurs half-year interest and excess-cash repayments occur at year-end.

Bear/base/bull terminal prices are ₹68.01/₹545.06/₹1,514.99, with annualized returns −31.86%/3.32%/26.76%. Peak debt is ₹205.31/₹288.91/₹379.46 crore, exceeding the ₹125 crore facility-description reference by ₹80.31/₹163.91/₹254.46 crore. The reference is not guaranteed drawable capacity; bank guarantees and collateral consume headroom. Base 12%/15%/18% hurdle entries are ₹309.28/₹270.99/₹238.25. These are conditional mathematical outputs, not actionable buy limits.

The 3×3 margin/multiple table re-solves funding, rather than holding debt fixed. A 7× exit at base margin gives −7.91%; 9% margin and 7× gives −20.08%. Reducing WC to 45% yields 5.08%; recovering all terminal collateral yields only 5.92%. A separate 25% fresh-equity case at entry price adds cash and shares together, cutting peak debt to ₹118.19 crore but producing only 4.15% annual return. Main cases do not assume this rescue. Minorities are allocated to modeled existing subsidiary economics; foreign growth profits are excluded, and a larger minority deduction is separately tested.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: A credible loss path combines weak order renewal, delayed collections, inventory obsolescence and warranty claims with on-demand debt. Bear growth slows to 5%, margin to 9%, WC rises to 55%, collateral to 11%, and a ₹9.22 crore combined collectible-inventory/receivable haircut is funded without a second cash charge. Terminal equity falls to about ₹68 per share, an 85.3% loss from ₹463; peak debt is ₹205.31 crore. A severe demand/collection case leaves zero common equity and requires ₹304.70 crore peak debt. These are conditional stresses, not assertions of present insolvency. The July CARE upgrade on ₹55 crore rated facilities, current bank relationships and October promoter cash are material contrary evidence. They do not guarantee funding for the base growth plan, and the chairman’s personal dispute is not assumed to attach CLN assets. Stress funding, not a high growth label, determines downside resilience.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: At ₹463 and granted-option dilution, 5×/10× require terminal equity of ₹2538.00/₹5076.01 crore. The funded bull ends at ₹1,514.99 per share, only about 3.27×, and therefore does not establish 5×, let alone 10×. At unchanged multiples, fivefold/tenfold earnings in five years require 38.0%/58.5% CAGR, before additional dilution or financing leakage. Revenue expansion is not enough when advances, collateral, tax, warranties and overseas capital consume cash. More aggressive operating or multiple assumptions would need new evidence; no success probability or multibagger promise is assigned.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: At each result/filing, monitor eight concrete items: manufacturing versus trading/service growth and customer concentration; collection of the ₹97.63 crore good receivables and supplier advances; finished-goods ageing and actual warranty utilization; net tax/employee settlement without rolling old liabilities indefinitely; cash versus collateral deposits and accrued interest; actual bank utilization, guarantee sublimits and sanction increases against the ₹288.91 crore base peak; overseas capital and Egypt/Dubai operational progress without duplicate funding; and October share listing, ESOP vesting, management succession and any separately verified personal-dispute consequence. For execution, refresh BSE surveillance, lot, live spread and actual position capacity. A lower quote alone is not proof of improvement; improved cash realization or a funded growth plan is more important.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Avoid at the dated reference valuation. This is a high-growth manufacturer with moderate quality, weak cash realization and meaningful recapitalization dependence, not a verified compounder or an allegation-driven exclusion. The conditional IAS reflects inadequate base return and severe funded downside despite a possible favorable bull path. Sustained collection improvement, restrained capital requirements or a materially lower price could alter the assessment. The present ₹5 lakh reference is not a recommended allocation; an existing-holder decision also depends on portfolio exposure and executable exit conditions.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: The prospectus and original annual financial statements provide the historical and opening-claim record. Subsequent issuer allotment, rating, overseas, option, management and personal-dispute filings update the perimeter; original mirrors are identified where BSE retrieval was unavailable. Secondary OHLCV is clearly labeled and dated, rather than passed off as official current turnover. Primary peers are compared on matched FY26 operating economics, not stale quote multiples. The model’s main unresolved facts are actual interim cash, bank/guarantee headroom, foreign capital remittance allocation, FD availability and collection, warranty outcomes and precise current legal consequences. Sensitivities bound these economically without pretending that a model is a bank commitment. Current tax, employee claims, operating provisions, minority interests and potential dilution are each mapped once.

ranking_eligibility.reason: Numeric conditional research scores, with date/source/position assumptions retained; not execution approval or a recommendation to buy.

GOV.reason: Promoter subscribed ₹10.575 crore at disclosed terms and actual subsidiary loans were modest. Contrary evidence: broad prospective funding authorizations and deferred subsidiary-loan terms need oversight; personal chairman dispute is disclosed and not attributed to the issuer. No automatic critical gate.

MOAT.reason: Battery-pack engineering, product qualification and in-house manufacturing mix offer capability beyond trading. Contrary evidence: concentrated customers/suppliers, imported cells and warranty exposure do not establish a cell-chemistry or brand moat.

REV.reason: Core three-year revenue CAGR around 39% maps to 9, capped at 8 for 2–4-year comparable history. Subsidiary revenue of ₹0.555 crore cannot explain the ₹127.33 crore increase; FY24–26 manufacturing mix strengthens trajectory. Contrary evidence: fire-distorted profit history and concentrated orders; no five-year organic score claimed.

DUR.reason: Telecom backup, battery replacement and energy storage have multiyear demand; service/R&D mix complements packs. Contrary evidence: technology/cell-price changes, warranty obligations and unproven new overseas operations limit durability.

CAP.reason: Core NOPAT on a broad average debt-plus-equity-minus-free-cash base is about 14.4%, within a reasoned 12–16% capital-cost range rather than clear excess return. Collateral, supplier-advance funding and overseas investment absorb capital despite modest historical physical capex. Positive operating profit and equity cash support reinvestment, but do not prove a high incremental return.

CASH.reason: Two consecutive large operating outflows total ₹112.71 crore against ₹33.47 crore PAT, with borrowing replacing supplier/customer financing. This is persistent recent funding dependence, not merely capex. Contrary evidence: FY22–24 cash generation was positive and receivables over six months are limited. Reassess cap if collection/payable cycle normalizes.

BAL.reason: Short-term borrowings of ₹93.49 crore against ₹1.495 crore usable cash are refinancing-dependent. Base peak debt of ₹288.91 crore exceeds the ₹125 crore facility-description reference, while the separate 25% equity case reduces peak debt to ₹118.19 crore with dilution. Existing facilities, the rating upgrade and October cash provide counterevidence to immediate failure, not promised incremental credit.

EXEC.reason: Manufacturing revenue nearly doubled and small subsidiaries do not explain most growth. Contrary evidence: working-capital funding, product-warranty execution and new overseas manufacturing remain unproved at scale.

EARN.reason: PAT growth is supported by manufacturing mix, but cash divergence, warranty estimates and fire/insurance comparatives warrant discount. Contrary evidence: provisioned doubtful debt and original audited statements provide usable earnings evidence; no material adverse audit conclusion assumed.

R.reason: The dated ₹463 reference and full funded base produce 3.32% annualized return, 11.68 percentage points below the assumed 15% hurdle, mapping to R 1. Zero FD cash interest or full pledged-principal recovery do not reach the hurdle. The optimistic bull path is not substituted for the base.

D.reason: The credible bear ends near ₹68 per diluted share, approximately 85% below entry, and requires peak debt of ₹205 crore. Severe equity is zero. Current cash, fresh promoter equity and bank/rating evidence are contrary evidence to immediate failure, but do not establish stress funding.

P.reason: An 18% growth, 11% margin and 10× exit reference still falls short of the hurdle. A 7× exit at base margin gives a negative return; a high-growth, higher-margin bull is needed for strong upside. Several optimistic assumptions must hold together, although the historical manufacturing expansion makes growth possible rather than inherently implausible.

L.reason: Observed 60-session median bounds imply roughly 11–12 sessions at 5% participation, a starting score of 3. Downgrade one point because the ₹92,600 lot is 18.52% of the ₹5 lakh reference position and exceeds 5% of typical daily turnover; four single-price observations also constrain flexibility. Missing-day bounds do not erase the >10-session result. No suspension is inferred.

gates.reason: No substantiated shareholder abuse identified; personal commercial dispute remains separately attributed and contested. RPT terms and current legal consequences require monitoring.

Original audited statements and claim notes support a bounded model. Minor drafting/rounding issues are not treated as a material reliability failure. Actual interim cash and restricted deposit releases remain unknown.

The base growth path requires substantial additional borrowing beyond the disclosed facility reference, not proven available. Existing banking, new equity and a lower-debt recapitalization sensitivity prevent calling a current unfinanceable shortfall or default established.

Dated secondary trades and official lot/market category support limited capacity estimates. Missing observations, lot constraints and unavailable live spread/BSE surveillance details preclude execution assurance.

conventions: March audited balance sheet with October allotment cash added once during FY27; no invented actual October balance sheet. Five fiscal years plus terminal stub are conditional operating paths over a five-year investor valuation horizon.
New debt has half-year interest; excess cash repayments occur at year-end. Positive-profit tax and draw are solved jointly. Forecast borrowing is required funding, not approved headroom.

Income-tax provision is explicitly net of TDS. Settle ₹8.529 crore once, without deducting a second unsubstantiated advance-tax offset. GST recoverable is operating working capital, not income-tax cash.

Current employee liabilities are paid once outside WC. Ordinary current statutory/expense/customer liabilities and warranty reserve are inside opening and forecast WC and never separately settled. Future warranty and compensation accruals remain within forecast margins and working-capital changes.

Retain net noncurrent gratuity/absence and rent-equalization claims in terminal equity. Existing plan assets are already netted. Equity-settled ESOP reserve is not cash debt; granted options receive both shares and exercise cash. Main case assumes all granted options exercised during FY27; no-exercise sensitivity is provided.

Use ₹17 crore conditional aggregate overseas spend, with ₹10/25 crore bounds. This includes the Dubai-to-Egypt chain rather than adding both amounts; it is not a claimed exact USD conversion. No unverified foreign profits, book value or terminal recovery is added.

All ₹33.3728 crore deposits are unavailable in the main case. Additional collateral grows with revenue and is cash-funded. Interest is separated from operations with 0–100% cash collection sensitivity. Principal and old-interest recoveries appear only in separate cases.

Tiny CLNGreen minority is valued using 49% of its FY26 revenue share and the same forecast economics; overseas incremental profit is excluded. A separate 1% whole-group EV minority case tests greater leakage. This is a valuation allocation assumption, not an asserted exact subsidiary equity valuation.

₹125 crore is the sum of disclosed cash-credit facility descriptions, not guaranteed drawable headroom; it includes guarantees and collateral conditions. Peak debt above that reference requires additional finance.
No dividends or fresh rescue shares in core cases; 25% equity case funds cash and dilution together. Asset haircuts reduce collectible opening WC without a second cash charge or assumed tax benefit.
